1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e3.strategy: Completes the kingside development and guards d4 and e5, so the centre is firm before anything is decided. White keeps every plan open, from a slow build-up to an exchange on d5, while Black, with both knights and the bishop out, will want to castle and then look for ways to free a cramped position.

Castles into safety and completes Black's standard set-up: the pawns on d5 and e6 hold the centre and every piece stands behind them. The price is a cramped game, since the c8-bishop is shut in behind the e6-pawn. Black has to free the position by exchanging pieces or striking at the centre later, while White has more space.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e3.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Defence
